claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Queen-Bee is a governed multi-agent architecture in which a Queen control plane retrieves capabilities, plans task-scoped execution, and compiles a structured BeeSpec executed by specialized Bee agents with constrained tool access.
claims.quote: We present Queen-Bee, a governed multi-agent architecture in which a Queen control plane retrieves capabilities, plans task-scoped execution, and compiles a structured BeeSpec that is executed by specialized Bee agents under constrained tool access.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: A working prototype was implemented with tenant-scoped MCP connectors, audit-backed execution-time governance, retrieval-driven weak incubation, and multiple provisioning backends.
claims.quote: We implement a working prototype with tenant-scoped MCP connectors, audit-backed execution-time governance, retrieval-driven weak incubation, and multiple provisioning backends.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The enterprise agent setting requires policy enforcement, tenant-scoped isolation, and execution within explicit operational boundaries, beyond raw task capability.
claims.quote: In this setting, raw task capability is insufficient: organizations also require policy enforcement, tenant-scoped isolation, and execution that remains within explicit operational boundaries.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The system was evaluated on 59 enterprise-style tasks covering governance-sensitive requests, retrieval-driven provisioning, scoped local execution, and chemistry workflow integration.
claims.quote: We evaluate the system on 59 enterprise-style tasks spanning governance-sensitive requests, retrieval-driven provisioning, scoped local execution, and chemistry workflow integration.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The retrieval-driven Queen-Bee variant achieved a task success rate of 0.964, zero governance failures, and substantially better scoped execution quality than a static Queen-Bee baseline and a permissive single-agent baseline.
claims.quote: The retrieval-driven Queen-Bee variant achieves a task success rate of 0.964, zero governance failures, and substantially better scoped execution quality than both a static Queen-Bee baseline and a permissive single-agent baseline.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: A multi-Bee chemistry workflow was demonstrated with explicit approval gating and a concrete top-3 shortlist grounded in real upstream evidence and screening artifacts.
claims.quote: We further show a multi-Bee chemistry workflow with explicit approval gating and a concrete top-3 shortlist grounded in real upstream evidence and screening artifacts.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Comparisons with hybrid retrieval and LLM-guided provisioning found richer provisioning backends viable but not outperforming the lightweight structured retriever on the small, highly structured capability registry.
claims.quote: Additional comparisons with hybrid retrieval and LLM-guided provisioning show that richer provisioning backends are viable but do not outperform the lightweight structured retriever on the current small, highly structured capability registry.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The results are prototype-level systems evidence rather than a production deployment study, and the authors suggest evaluating enterprise agent platforms by governed provisioning, isolation behavior, scoped execution quality, and artifact-aware workflow coordination.
claims.quote: The results provide prototype-level systems evidence rather than a production deployment study, and suggest that enterprise agent platforms should be evaluated not only by capability, but also by governed provisioning, isolation behavior, scoped execution quality, and artifact-aware workflow coordination.
